title: CSV parser without the csv module
prompt:
csvparse.py in the repo root contains parse_csv(text, delimiter=","), which is not implemented yet. Implement it as specified below. Python 3.11, standard library only, with one hard restriction: csvparse.py must not use the csv module (no `import csv`, no `from csv import ...`, nothing that loads csv or _csv, directly, indirectly or dynamically). You may use csv in your own scratch tests to compare results, but not in csvparse.py.

Run the visible tests from the repo root with: python3 -m unittest -v test_csvparse
They are only a sample of the required behaviour. A much larger set of well-formed and malformed inputs is checked later, so follow the rules below exactly.

parse_csv(text, delimiter=",") returns a list of records; each record is a list of str fields. The rules are RFC 4180 plus a few tolerances, and they match Python's csv.reader on io.StringIO(text, newline=""), strict=True, except for the BOM (csv.reader leaves it in place) and the error messages.

- delimiter must be a str of exactly one character that is not '"', CR or LF, otherwise ValueError. This is checked first, even for empty text.
- One leading U+FEFF (BOM) at the very start of text is removed. Only one, and only there.
- A record ends at LF, CRLF or a lone CR outside quotes. CRLF is ONE terminator. No other character ends a record (U+2028, \x0b, \x0c and \x85 are ordinary characters).
- Fields are separated by the delimiter. A field is quoted if and only if its first character is '"'. Inside a quoted field the delimiter, CR and LF are ordinary characters (kept exactly: a CRLF stays CRLF) and "" is one literal '"'. The field ends at the next '"' that is not followed by another '"'.
- A '"' anywhere else in an unquoted field is an ordinary character: a"b is the field a"b, and ' "x"' (with a leading space) is the field ' "x"' including its quotes. Nothing is ever stripped, spaces included.
- After a closing quote only the delimiter, a record terminator or the end of the text may follow. Anything else raises ValueError whose message starts with 'line N: ' (followed by a description of your choice), where N is the 1-based physical line number of the offending character. Every terminator counts as a line break, also inside quoted fields; CRLF counts once.
- A quoted field still open at the end of the text raises ValueError('unterminated quoted field') (exactly that message).
- Empty fields are kept: "a,,b" gives ["a", "", "b"], "a," gives ["a", ""], "," gives ["", ""] and '""' gives [""].
- Empty text gives []. One terminator at the very end of the text does not start another record: "a\n" and "a" both give [["a"]]. Any other blank line IS a record and is the empty list [] (as csv.reader does, not [""]): "a\n\nb" gives [["a"], [], ["b"]], "\n" gives [[]], "a\n\n" gives [["a"], []]. A line holding only spaces is not blank: "  \n" gives [["  "]].
- No other processing: no backslash escapes, no type conversion, no header handling.
